## Load libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
library("table1")
```

## Data Description

The taxamony, meta, as well as the ASV dataset were sourced from the GEO series GSE311689, a study by the Biological Networks Laboratory at the University of San Sebastian. The study, titled "SARS-CoV-2 Variant-Dependent Alterations in Nasopharyngeal Microbiota and Host Inflammatory Response" and published on the 30th of January 2026, aimed to characterize variant-associatiod changes in nasopharyngeal microbial communities during SARS-CoV-2 infection. For this study 300 nasopharyngeal swabs were collected in Chile between April 2021 and August 2021 for SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis and variant identification. The cytokine expression was quantified by RT-qPCR and variants (Gamma, Lambda, Delta) were determined using Hydrolusys Probe-based assays. Bacterial community profiling was performed by sequencing the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene using Illumina MiSeq technology. Amplicon sequence variants (ASV) were identified by processing raw sequencing reads using the DADA2 pipeline.

## Cohort Definition

The study cohort comprises 300 nasopharyngeal swab samples stratified into SARS-CoV-2-negative controls ($n = 71$, 23.7%) and three SARS-CoV-2 variant groups: Gamma ($n = 88$, 29.3%), Lambda ($n = 78$, 26.0%), and Delta ($n = 63$, 21.0%). Overall, gender is evenly distributed with 145 females (48.3%) and 155 males (51.7%), though sex proportions vary across groups—ranging from 38.6% female in Gamma to 60.3% female in Delta. Patient age spans from 0 to 100 years, with a cohort-wide median of 40.0 years (mean 43.1 $\pm$ 24.5 years) and comparable median ages across all four groups (37.0 to 41.5 years). Geographically, samples originate from 14 municipalities (*comunas*) within the Santiago Metropolitan Region, with the majority collected in San Bernardo ($n = 96$, 32.0%), La Florida ($n = 84$, 28.0%), El Bosque ($n = 53$, 17.7%), and Pedro Aguirre Cerda ($n = 32$, 10.7%).

```{r}
meta_clean |>
  mutate(Gender = factor(sex),
         Cohort = factor(variant)) |>
  table1(x = formula(~ sex + age + city|variant),
         data = _)
```

## Confounding variables

Nasopharyngeal swabs were collected in Chile between April and August 2021. Temporal distribution was uneven across groups, with no SARS-CoV-2-negative control samples collected during April and May, indicating potential confounding by sampling time. Because our goal is to characterize SARS-CoV-2 variant-dependent changes in the nasopharyngeal microbiota, the absence of SARS-CoV-2-negative controls during April and May prevents a direct baseline comparison of how the infected microbiota shifted relative to an uninfected state during those months. By removing the months April and May the confounder can be avoided,

```{r}
meta_aug |>
  count(month, variant) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variant, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

```

## Plots to make the description section easier to visualize

## Load libraries

```{r}
#| message: false
library("tidyverse")
source("99_proj_func.R")
```

## Load data

```{r}
dat_aug <- read_tsv(file = "../data/03_dat_aug.tsv") |>
  set_factor_levels()
```

`03_dat_aug.tsv` has one row per sample and ASV. Sample-level variables
(metadata, cytokines, read QC and diversity) are repeated in every row of a
sample, so for describing the samples we keep one row per sample.

```{r}
dat_samples <- dat_aug |>
  select(-c(asv_id, reads, rel_abund, kingdom:species)) |>
  distinct()

dat_samples |>
  count(sample_id) |>
  filter(n > 1) |>
  nrow()
```

# 1. The cohort

## 1.1 Samples per group

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  count(result, variant) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

## 1.2 Age and sex per group

```{r}
cohort_table <- dat_samples |>
  group_by(variant) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            age_median = median(age),
            age_q1 = quantile(age, probs = 0.25),
            age_q3 = quantile(age, probs = 0.75),
            pct_female = round(100 * mean(sex == "Female"), 1))

cohort_table
```

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = variant,
                       y = age,
                       fill = variant)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6,
               outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2,
              size = 1,
              alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = variant_colours) +
  labs(title = "Age distribution per group",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Age (years)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = variant,
                       fill = age_group)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ sex) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues") +
  labs(title = "Age group and sex composition per group",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Share of samples",
       fill = "Age group") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 2. When the samples were collected

The variants circulated at different times, so sampling date may be
confounded with variant. This plot shows how the groups are distributed over
the sampling period.

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  count(month, variant) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variant,
              values_from = n,
              values_fill = 0)
```

```{r}
key_plot_calendar <- dat_samples |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = month,
                       fill = variant)) +
  geom_bar(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single"),
           colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = variant_colours) +
  labs(title = "Samples collected per month and group (2021)",
       subtitle = "No SARS-CoV-2 negative samples were collected in April or May",
       x = "Month of collection",
       y = "Number of samples",
       fill = "Group") +
  theme_minimal()

key_plot_calendar

ggsave(filename = "../results/04_key_plot_1.png",
       plot = key_plot_calendar,
       width = 8,
       height = 5,
       dpi = 300)
```

# 3. Sequencing quality

## 3.1 Sequencing depth

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  select(variant, total_reads, bacterial_reads) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(total_reads, bacterial_reads),
               names_to = "read_type",
               values_to = "reads") |>
  group_by(read_type) |>
  summarise(min = min(reads),
            median = median(reads),
            max = max(reads))
```

## 3.2 Non-bacterial reads

Eukaryotic (host), unassigned, chloroplast and mitochondrial reads were removed
in `03_augment`. Their share differs a lot between samples.

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  group_by(variant) |>
  summarise(median_pct_non_bacterial = median(pct_non_bacterial),
            max_pct_non_bacterial = max(pct_non_bacterial))
```

```{r}
key_plot_qc <- dat_samples |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = variant,
                       y = pct_non_bacterial,
                       fill = variant)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6,
               outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2,
              size = 1,
              alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = variant_colours) +
  labs(title = "Share of non-bacterial reads removed per sample",
       subtitle = "Mostly eukaryotic (host) DNA",
       x = NULL,
       y = "Non-bacterial reads (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

key_plot_qc

ggsave(filename = "../results/04_key_plot_2.png",
       plot = key_plot_qc,
       width = 7,
       height = 5,
       dpi = 300)
```

# 4. Cytokines

## 4.1 Missing values and flagged samples

```{r}
dat_samples |>
  summarise(across(.cols = c(il2, ifn_g, tnf_a, il1ra),
                   .fns = ~ sum(is.na(.x))))

dat_samples |>
  count(variant, qc_cytokine_duplicated) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = qc_cytokine_duplicated,
              values_from = n,
              values_fill = 0,
              names_prefix = "duplicated_")
```

## 4.2 Why a log scale

Cytokine values span many orders of magnitude, so on a linear scale almost all
samples pile up near zero. On a log10 scale the distributions become
interpretable.

```{r}
cytokines_long <- dat_samples |>
  select(sample_id, variant, il2, ifn_g, tnf_a, il1ra) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(il2, ifn_g, tnf_a, il1ra),
               names_to = "cytokine",
               values_to = "expression") |>
  drop_na(expression) |>
  mutate(cytokine = case_match(cytokine,
                               "il2" ~ "IL-2",
                               "ifn_g" ~ "IFN-gamma",
                               "tnf_a" ~ "TNF-alpha",
                               "il1ra" ~ "IL-1ra"))

cytokines_long |>
  group_by(cytokine) |>
  summarise(min = min(expression),
            median = median(expression),
            max = max(expression),
            orders_of_magnitude = log10(max / min))
```

```{r}
cytokines_long |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40,
                 fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ cytokine,
             scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Cytokine expression on a linear scale",
       x = "Relative expression",
       y = "Number of samples") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
key_plot_cytokines <- cytokines_long |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40,
                 fill = "steelblue") +
  facet_wrap(~ cytokine) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_log()) +
  labs(title = "Cytokine expression on a log10 scale",
       x = "Relative expression (log10 scale)",
       y = "Number of samples") +
  theme_minimal()

key_plot_cytokines

ggsave(filename = "../results/04_key_plot_3.png",
       plot = key_plot_cytokines,
       width = 8,
       height = 5,
       dpi = 300)
```

# 5. The bacterial community

## 5.1 Taxonomic overview

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  filter(reads > 0) |>
  summarise(n_asv = n_distinct(asv_id),
            n_genus = n_distinct(genus),
            n_family = n_distinct(family),
            n_phylum = n_distinct(phylum))
```

## 5.2 Most abundant phyla and genera

Mean relative abundance across all samples (each sample weighs the same).

```{r}
dat_aug |>
  group_by(sample_id, phylum) |>
  summarise(rel_abund = sum(rel_abund),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(phylum) |>
  summarise(mean_pct = 100 * mean(rel_abund)) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_pct))
```

```{r}
top_genera <- dat_aug |>
  group_by(sample_id, genus) |>
  summarise(rel_abund = sum(rel_abund),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(genus) |>
  summarise(mean_pct = 100 * mean(rel_abund),
            prevalence_pct = 100 * mean(rel_abund > 0)) |>
  slice_max(order_by = mean_pct,
            n = 15)

top_genera
```

```{r}
top_genera |>
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = mean_pct,
                       y = fct_reorder(genus, mean_pct))) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "15 most abundant bacterial genera (all samples)",
       x = "Mean relative abundance (%)",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```
